1. Key Step: Have Chompy sweep the olives and pinecones with the small flame at the tip of its tail until the pinecone shell cracks open with a “pop,” and the olive aroma wafts out naturally.
2. Mixing: Finely crush the roasted pine nuts and olives, stir in granulated sugar and crushed hazelnuts, then sprinkle a pinch of seasoning powder to bring out the flavor.
3. Shaping: Knead flour into small dough balls, fold in the mixture, and press flat using a claw mark mold.
4. Egg Wash: Brush on a thin, even layer—smooth as sunset spilling across the sea.
5. Baking: Bake slowly until the egg wash turns golden brown; reposition the baking tray halfway through.
6. Tasting: Since Chompy owns this secret recipe, the very first fresh-baked bite goes to Chompy, Chief Taster!

1. According to Institute observations, Vein energy has recently become unusually active in certain areas, bringing special changes to the local ecosystems.
2. During the event, for your first 3 Nurtures each weekend in the designated areas, the chance of Nova Stage Aniimo appearing is greatly increased, and Prismatic Energy gained from picking Veinfruit is increased by an extra 50%. 
Nurturing increases the current area’s Prismatic Energy, and catching Aniimo also has a chance to trigger a Lucky Strike that further increases it.
· Each Nurturing increases an area’s Prismatic Energy, and there’s a 3% chance to trigger a Prismana Flow, drawing out that area’s Prismana Aniimo. 
· Each time a Lucky Strike occurs while catching Aniimo, increasing a region’s Prismatic Energy, there’s a 0.6% chance a Prismana Flow will trigger, drawing out that area’s Prismana Aniimo.
3. Every weekend, the abundant Vein energy will also draw large numbers of Aniimo to the designated areas for you to explore and catch.

1. According to Institute observations, Vein energy has recently become unusually active in certain areas, bringing special changes to the local ecosystems.
2. During the event, for your first 3 Nurtures each weekend in the designated areas, the chance of Nova Stage Aniimo appearing is greatly increased, and Prismatic Energy gained from picking Veinfruit is increased by an extra 50%. 
Nurturing increases the current area’s Prismatic Energy, and catching Aniimo also has a chance to trigger a Lucky Strike that further increases it.
· Each Nurturing increases an area’s Prismatic Energy, and there’s a 3% chance to trigger a Prismana Flow, drawing out that area’s Prismana Aniimo. 
· Each time a Lucky Strike occurs while catching Aniimo, increasing a region’s Prismatic Energy, there’s a 0.6% chance a Prismana Flow will trigger, drawing out that area’s Prismana Aniimo.
3. Every weekend, the abundant Vein energy will also draw large numbers of Aniimo to the designated areas for you to explore and catch.

1. According to Institute observations, Vein energy has recently become unusually active in certain areas, bringing special changes to the local ecosystems.
2. During the event, for your first 3 Nurtures each weekend in the designated areas, the chance of Nova Stage Aniimo appearing is greatly increased, and Prismatic Energy gained from picking Veinfruit is increased by an extra 50%. 
Nurturing increases the current area’s Prismatic Energy, and catching Aniimo also has a chance to trigger a Lucky Strike that further increases it.
· Each Nurturing increases an area’s Prismatic Energy, and there’s a 3% chance to trigger a Prismana Flow, drawing out that area’s Prismana Aniimo. 
· Each time a Lucky Strike occurs while catching Aniimo, increasing a region’s Prismatic Energy, there’s a 0.6% chance a Prismana Flow will trigger, drawing out that area’s Prismana Aniimo.
3. Every weekend, the abundant Vein energy will also draw large numbers of Aniimo to the designated areas for you to explore and catch.

Long ago, a challenger passed the Three Trials of the Rapids and became the greatest warrior of the Tidesung Fleet. They trudged through sucking mud, fought through roaring torrents, climbed to heights beyond their old limits—and found the path thrilling and meaningful. So they turned it into a trial, so those who came after could prove their strength the same way. It was an era of honor and ocean exploration; every greatest warrior forged their legacy on this path.
Then disaster struck. The fleet scattered, and its glory faded into legend. She revived the trials, hoping to gather a new fleet, sail through storms, and chart the farthest seas. Yet what followed taught her that mortal strength has its bounds. Now she lives quietly in Mirrorsea Village, just another elder laughing at old memories. Only her companion, an unfathomable Royalby, tends to the forgotten trial.

During the event, Pathfinders can participate in the Night Candy House and Night Perfume Making events to collect stickers, fill out the Night Journal, and claim parade rewards.
[Night Candy House]

1. Complete daily Parade quests to earn Night Candies, up to 3 per day. Candies can be saved up with no limits.
2. Spend Night Candies on the main event page to decorate the Candy House and receive a gift. After spending 30 Candies in total, the Candy House will be fully decorated.

[Night Perfume Making]
1. Aniimo companions will visit one after another during the event. Make a perfume for each visitor in the order they arrive. Aniimo that have already visited will remain available until the event ends.
2. Based on each visiting Aniimo’s preferences, choose 3 ingredients from those offered to make a perfume. If the fragrance meets the requirements, you can submit it to receive rewards and an Aniimo sticker. If it doesn’t meet the requirements, you cannot submit it.

[Night Journal]
1. Decorate the Candy House and make perfume for visitors to obtain corresponding Journal stickers. Collect enough stickers to claim the corresponding rewards.

Step 1: Blow long vs. short
Long tone —: continuous and sustained, with steady breath.
Short tone ·: quick and crisp, cutting the airflow off in time.

Step 2: Blow high vs. low
Rising pitch ↗: lift the tail end; used for questions and calling out.
Falling pitch ↘: slow your breath and drop the tail end; used for replies and confirmation.

Step 3: Add a swipe tone
On the basis of a long tone, slowly open and close your palm to let the pitch glide smoothly up or down!

Common village whistle-speech
A continuous long tone — is used to call your Aniimo companion.
A fast, bright beat · — is used during transport to communicate the direction of movement.
A rapid beat · · · · is used to quickly seek help.
A gliding beat ... is used to express sincere wishes.

...
If you want to learn whistle-speech, start by making a sound—and then blowing the pitch.

1407520249:
Dear Mr. Harvey,
Your letter was wonderful. Mirrorsea Village sounds like such a special place, and I’m really interested in those Aniimo you described: a bubble-spitting octopus, a singing Dewlop, and that Hypnowl? Named Vivi? It sounds a lot like my partner—except mine can’t hypnotize anyone. I reread your last reply so many times it felt like I’d traveled right along with you to that seaside village.
My life at the institute is nowhere near as fun as yours. It’s either classes or lab work, and last week the professor even docked points. I seriously don’t get it—how is turning my silly partner into a balloon ""disrupting class order""?
I truly appreciate you writing back. You probably don’t know this, but opening a letter from the seaside in a quiet corner of the library is the thing I look forward to most each week. It makes me feel like there’s a bigger world out there—so strange and wonderful, like another world entirely.
Oh, and that question you asked last time—about how to start talking to strangers—I think you’ve already found your answer. You and I started with a letter, didn’t we?
I’ve enclosed a few honey candies. I hope their sweetness pairs well with the sea breeze on your end.
Looking forward to your next letter.
Your pen pal, Tom
From Platform 9¾

1. According to Institute observations, Vein energy has recently become unusually active in certain areas, bringing special changes to the local ecosystems.
2. During the event, for your first 3 Nurtures each weekend in the designated areas, the chance of Nova Stage Aniimo appearing is greatly increased, and Prismatic Energy gained from picking Veinfruit is increased by an extra 50%. 
Nurturing increases the current area’s Prismatic Energy, and catching Aniimo also has a chance to trigger a Lucky Strike that further increases it.
· Each Nurturing increases an area’s Prismatic Energy, and there’s a 3% chance to trigger a Prismana Flow, drawing out that area’s Prismana Aniimo. 
· Each time a Lucky Strike occurs while catching Aniimo, increasing a region’s Prismatic Energy, there’s a 0.6% chance a Prismana Flow will trigger, drawing out that area’s Prismana Aniimo.
3. Every weekend, the abundant Vein energy will also draw large numbers of Aniimo to the designated areas for you to explore and catch.
4. During the event, certain special Prismana Aniimo will also be drawn by the Vein energy and appear in designated areas for a limited time. See the event schedule below for details on which Prismana Forms appear in which areas at each stage.

Prismana Form Pouchwisp appears in Rosy Mirelands and Tideblossom Coast.

1. Once the event begins, Polaris Institute will reveal this period’s mystery Aniimo silhouette.
2. The initial silhouette will only show the mystery Aniimo’s distinctive features, with the remaining parts hidden. Pathfinders can reveal the hidden parts by photographing Aniimo that share the same features as the mystery Aniimo.
3. Photograph an Aniimo matching the silhouette’s corresponding form and submit the photo to complete the research topic and claim the corresponding rewards. Successfully photographing the mystery Aniimo before the full silhouette is revealed earns you bonus Aniimo Observation Rewards!
4. Pathfinders can also select photos from their existing album that meet the topic requirements for submission. If a photo contains this period’s mystery Aniimo, it counts toward event completion too.
5. Pay attention to Aniimo forms — only photos where the submitted Aniimo matches the mystery Aniimo’s exact form will count toward event completion.
6. Pathfinders can complete the event by photographing their own Aniimo, other players’ Aniimo, or wild Aniimo on the continent of Idyll.
7. Aniimo in the Holo-Battle Sim are holographic projections, and Aniimo found in Sanctums are bound by ancient seals. Photos taken in these two locations cannot be recognized or submitted.

1. According to Institute observations, Vein energy has recently become unusually active in certain areas, bringing special changes to the local ecosystems.
2. During the event, for your first 3 Nurtures each weekend in the designated areas, the chance of Nova Stage Aniimo appearing is greatly increased, and Prismatic Energy gained from picking Veinfruit is increased by an extra 50%. 
Nurturing increases the current area’s Prismatic Energy, and catching Aniimo also has a chance to trigger a Lucky Strike that further increases it.
· Each Nurturing increases an area’s Prismatic Energy, and there’s a 3% chance to trigger a Prismana Flow, drawing out that area’s Prismana Aniimo. 
· Each time a Lucky Strike occurs while catching Aniimo, increasing a region’s Prismatic Energy, there’s a 0.6% chance a Prismana Flow will trigger, drawing out that area’s Prismana Aniimo.
3. Every weekend, the abundant Vein energy will also draw large numbers of Aniimo to the designated areas for you to explore and catch.
4. During the event, certain special Prismana Aniimo will also be drawn by the Vein energy and appear in designated areas for a limited time. See the event schedule below for details on which Prismana Forms appear in which areas at each stage.

Preface:
If you’ve opened this book, it means you’ve taken an interest in Gu-speech—congratulations. Gu-speech is an ancient and beautiful language spoken by the Hypnowl. Its vocabulary is small, but its meanings are rich.

This book is written for beginners who want to communicate with the Hypnowl at a basic level. It contains five lessons, moving from simple to advanced in a steady progression. Lessons 1–5 cover greetings, questions, replies, eating, and everyday emotional expressions.

Each lesson includes: common Gu-speech phrases, usage scenarios, and pointers on common mistakes. Please note that Gu-speech has no standardized grammar rules, and different Hypnowls may have different pronunciation habits.

It’s recommended you study one lesson per day and practice in real situations.

During the writing of this book, we received help from many Hypnowls in Mirrorsea Village. Special thanks to Master Gu, who contributed about 80% of the example sentences in this book.

During the event, Pathfinders can participate in the Night Candy House and Night Perfume Making events to collect stickers, fill out the Night Journal, and claim parade rewards.
[Night Candy House]

1. Complete daily Parade quests to earn Night Candies, up to 3 per day. Candies can be saved up with no limits.
2. Spend Night Candies on the main event page to decorate the Candy House and receive a gift. After spending 30 Candies in total, the Candy House will be fully decorated.

[Night Perfume Making]
1. Aniimo companions will visit one after another during the event. Make a perfume for each visitor in the order they arrive. Aniimo that have already visited will remain available until the event ends.
2. Based on each visiting Aniimo’s preferences, choose 3 ingredients from those offered to make a perfume. If the fragrance meets the requirements, you can submit it to receive rewards and an Aniimo sticker. If it doesn’t meet the requirements, you cannot submit it.

[Night Journal]
1. Decorate the Candy House and make perfume for visitors to obtain corresponding Journal stickers. Collect enough stickers to claim the corresponding rewards.

1752894843:
Tesella Pod’s HQ is a magnet for wandering Aniimo. The folks who work here love Aniimo just as much as the students at Polaris Institute—see an Aniimo and they’ll reflexively pull out a can, the same way students reflexively pull out an Aniipod.

After a while, most Aniimo pick a feeder to twine with and stop roaming. But there’s one Morphling that refuses—no matter what—to choose a single, steady human partner. Even if someone takes it home, it’ll still turn up at Tesella Pod HQ the next day.

So people stopped fixating on twining with the Morphling and instead treated it like a close friend: eating, drinking, playing around, and spending the holidays together. And when it comes to changing shape, the Morphling really shows off. On the Harvest Festival, it turns into an apple, hides in a pile of fruit, and jumpscares someone with a “surprise.” On the Spooktacular Festival, it becomes a sparkling jack-o’-lantern, slyly waiting for the lucky soul who picks it up.

“A thousand-shapes Morphling is an Aniimo that bonds with the world,” said Ms. Amber, founder of Tesella Pod.

The Morphling found the phrase “bond with the world” fascinating. But the Astra hangs high in space—its world has four borders, utterly unlike the boundless Idyll.

It thought, “I should go see Idyll! That’s where I was born, too!”

Before leaving for Idyll, the Morphling decided it should say goodbye to the people at Tesella Pod. But when it came by again, the company was in the middle of a celebration. “Doesn’t feel like the right time to say goodbye,” it thought. So, like always, it joined the party and decided to go next time.

Next time, a female technician happened to make a beautiful plate of Aniimo-meal to feed it. “Ugh—saying goodbye now would totally kill the vibe!” So, like always, it finished the pretty meal and decided it would say it next time.

Next time, the time after next... it never seemed like the right moment. Maybe a young operator was crying over a breakup and needed the adorable Morphling to comfort them. Maybe a batch of new hires had just joined Tesella Pod and were building precious friendships with it. Either way, no day felt right—so every day became: “Ugh, next time for sure!”

...

And so, one morning—before the workday even began—the Morphling took off the mask that carried its memories and quietly set it down at Tesella Pod’s front door. With the mask removed, Astra faded from its memory, leaving only a warm, happy blur.

Free at last, the Morphling set out on its journey.

“After the trip is over, I’ll put it back on again!”

1. Once the event begins, Polaris Institute will reveal this period’s mystery Aniimo silhouette.
2. The initial silhouette will only show the mystery Aniimo’s distinctive features, with the remaining parts hidden. Pathfinders can reveal the hidden parts by photographing Aniimo that share the same features as the mystery Aniimo.
3. Photograph an Aniimo matching the silhouette’s corresponding form and submit the photo to complete the research topic and claim the corresponding rewards. Successfully photographing the mystery Aniimo before the full silhouette is revealed earns you bonus Aniimo Observation Rewards!
4. Pathfinders can also select photos from their existing album that meet the topic requirements for submission. If a photo contains this period’s mystery Aniimo, it counts toward event completion too.
5. Pay attention to Aniimo forms — only photos where the submitted Aniimo matches the mystery Aniimo’s exact form will count toward event completion.
6. Pathfinders can complete the event by photographing their own Aniimo, other players’ Aniimo, or wild Aniimo on the continent of Idyll.
7. Aniimo in the Holo-Battle Sim are holographic projections, and Aniimo found in Sanctums are bound by ancient seals. Photos taken in these two locations cannot be recognized or submitted.

Nurturing increases the current area’s Prismatic Energy, and catching Aniimo also has a chance to trigger a Lucky Strike that further increases it.
· Each Nurturing increases an area’s Prismatic Energy, and there’s a 3% chance to trigger a Prismana Flow, drawing out that area’s Prismana Aniimo.

1. Once the event begins, Polaris Institute will reveal this period’s mystery Aniimo silhouette.
2. The initial silhouette will only show the mystery Aniimo’s distinctive features, with the remaining parts hidden. Pathfinders can reveal the hidden parts by photographing Aniimo that share the same features as the mystery Aniimo.
3. Photograph an Aniimo matching the silhouette’s corresponding form and submit the photo to complete the research topic and claim the corresponding rewards. Successfully photographing the mystery Aniimo before the full silhouette is revealed earns you bonus Aniimo Observation Rewards!
4. Pathfinders can also select photos from their existing album that meet the topic requirements for submission. If a photo contains this period’s mystery Aniimo, it counts toward event completion too.
5. Pay attention to Aniimo forms — only photos where the submitted Aniimo matches the mystery Aniimo’s exact form will count toward event completion.
6. Pathfinders can complete the event by photographing their own Aniimo, other players’ Aniimo, or wild Aniimo on the continent of Idyll.
7. Aniimo in the Holo-Battle Sim are holographic projections, and Aniimo found in Sanctums are bound by ancient seals. Photos taken in these two locations cannot be recognized or submitted.

· Each Nurturing increases an area’s Prismatic Energy, and there’s a 3% chance to trigger a Prismana Flow, drawing out that area’s Prismana Aniimo.

During the event, Pathfinders can participate in the Night Candy House and Night Perfume Making events to collect stickers, fill out the Night Journal, and claim parade rewards.
[Night Candy House]

1. Complete daily Parade quests to earn Night Candies, up to 3 per day. Candies can be saved up with no limits.
2. Spend Night Candies on the main event page to decorate the Candy House and receive a gift. After spending 30 Candies in total, the Candy House will be fully decorated.

[Night Perfume Making]
1. Aniimo companions will visit one after another during the event. Make a perfume for each visitor in the order they arrive. Aniimo that have already visited will remain available until the event ends.
2. Based on each visiting Aniimo’s preferences, choose 3 ingredients from those offered to make a perfume. If the fragrance meets the requirements, you can submit it to receive rewards and an Aniimo sticker. If it doesn’t meet the requirements, you cannot submit it.

[Night Journal]
1. Decorate the Candy House and make perfume for visitors to obtain corresponding Journal stickers. Collect enough stickers to claim the corresponding rewards.

Pathfinder, welcome to this issue of the Companion Handbook! This issue’s featured Aniimo is <color=#da8000>Hypnyto</color>!
During your adventures out in the world, complete Companion Handbook quests, raise your Companion Handbook level, and earn superb Companion Handbook rewards!

Companion Handbook Editions
The Companion Handbook’s level progress rewards are divided into the Standard Edition and Advanced Edition. The Advanced Edition requires you to unlock the Advanced Companion Handbook. Rewards include 1 <color=#da8000>Prismana Hypnyto</color> with Perfect Potential, a <color=#da8000>Hypnyto Soul (an item used to evolve Hypnyto)</color>, and a range of other rewards. It also grants a special perk: More Aniimo storage boxes. The Advanced Edition adds 5 Aniimo storage boxes, while the Collector’s Edition adds 10. These capacity bonuses do not stack; whichever edition you activate last takes priority.
Unlocking the Collector’s Companion Handbook grants additional rewards and perks immediately on top of the Advanced Companion Handbook.

Quests and Companion Handbook EXP
Quests are divided into weekly quests and seasonal quests. Each quest can only be completed once, and there is no weekly EXP limit.
Weekly quests refresh every Monday at 04:00, with progress resetting each week. New Seasonal Quests are added to the quest pool every Monday and stay available for the rest of the season. Newly added quests remain locked until you finish prerequisite quests in their questline. All quests end when the current Companion Handbook ends.
Companion Handbook EXP can also be obtained from Institute Guide - Daily Activity.
Once the Companion Handbook passes Lv. 100, it switches to a repeating reward cycle that caps out at Lv. 1000.

Gift Details
You can send a gift to friends who meet the required Affinity and have not yet unlocked the Advanced or Collector’s Companion Handbook. They will receive 1 item that can activate either the Advanced or Collector’s Companion Handbook.

Rerun Details
The Prismana Aniimo Egg from this season’s Companion Handbook will return in Season 3, and will be obtainable through Home-related gameplay.

1. Once the event begins, Polaris Institute will reveal this period’s mystery Aniimo silhouette.
2. The initial silhouette will only show the mystery Aniimo’s distinctive features, with the remaining parts hidden. Pathfinders can reveal the hidden parts by photographing Aniimo that share the same features as the mystery Aniimo.
3. Photograph an Aniimo matching the silhouette’s corresponding form and submit the photo to complete the research topic and claim the corresponding rewards. Successfully photographing the mystery Aniimo before the full silhouette is revealed earns you bonus Aniimo Observation Rewards!
4. Pathfinders can also select photos from their existing album that meet the topic requirements for submission. If a photo contains this period’s mystery Aniimo, it counts toward event completion too.
5. Pay attention to Aniimo forms — only photos where the submitted Aniimo matches the mystery Aniimo’s exact form will count toward event completion.
6. Pathfinders can complete the event by photographing their own Aniimo, other players’ Aniimo, or wild Aniimo on the continent of Idyll.

Pathfinders can get Irisalis Petals in the following ways.
(Once the Tracing the Trail event ends, Irisalis Petals will no longer be available through that event.)

1. Story
Obtain by clearing the following Story chapters: Ceremony Preparations, The Unbegun Ceremony, Colorful Fragrance, The Land of Dancing Illusions, The Land where Dreams Come True, Ancient Sacred Fragrance, Rainbow of the Ground, and A New Journey.

2. Journey Quests
Obtain by clearing the following Journey Quests: The Legend of Mist and Light, The Legend of Echoback Landing, The Legend of Flowers and Thorns, The Legend of the Land of Falling Stars, The Legend of Thousand-Fang Ridge, The Legend of the Land of Lightning and Thunder, The Legend of Helmuts and Helgons, The Legend of the Bell of Freedom, The Legend of the Berylline Vale, and The Legend of Driftwise Meadow.

3. Open-World Gathering
Follow Irelia’s footsteps and gather Irisalis Petals across Breezy Plains.

4. First Alpha Clear
Get them upon your first victory over the Alpha in each area of Breezy Plains.

5. Elite Pathfinder Challenge
Obtain by defeating the following elite Pathfinders in Breezy Plains or Astra: Senior Wally, Senior Jilly, Senior Loulla, Senior Aster, Senior Wendell, Senior Cecelia, and Lita.

6. Branch Nurturing
Obtain by infusing energy into the Breezy Plains Branch and claiming its growth milestone rewards.

7. Breezy Plains Silver Badges
Obtain by claiming Silver Badges from each area in Breezy Plains.

8. Aniimo Research
Unlock the Nova Stage Aniimo Index entries for each Family in your Aniilog, complete the research topic Collect Prismana Form, and claim the corresponding rewards.

9. Tracing the Trail
Obtain from the limited-time event Tracing the Trail. Once the event ends, Irisalis Petals will no longer be available through this method.

Tesella Pod’s HQ is a magnet for wandering Aniimo. The folks who work here love Aniimo just as much as the students at Polaris Institute—see an Aniimo and they’ll reflexively pull out a can, the same way students reflexively pull out an Aniipod.

After a while, most Aniimo pick a feeder to twine with and stop roaming. But there’s one Morphling that refuses—no matter what—to choose a single, steady human partner. Even if someone takes it home, it’ll still turn up at Tesella Pod HQ the next day.

So people stopped fixating on twining with the Morphling and instead treated it like a close friend: eating, drinking, playing around, and spending the holidays together. And when it comes to changing shape, the Morphling really shows off. On the Harvest Festival, it turns into an apple, hides in a pile of fruit, and jumpscares someone with a “surprise.” On the Spooktacular Festival, it becomes a sparkling jack-o’-lantern, slyly waiting for the lucky soul who picks it up.

“A thousand-shapes Morphling is an Aniimo that bonds with the world,” said Ms. Amber, founder of Tesella Pod.

The Morphling found the phrase “bond with the world” fascinating. But the Astra hangs high in space—its world has four borders, utterly unlike the boundless Idyll.

It thought, “I should go see Idyll! That’s where I was born, too!”

Before leaving for Idyll, the Morphling decided it should say goodbye to the people at Tesella Pod. But when it came by again, the company was in the middle of a celebration. “Doesn’t feel like the right time to say goodbye,” it thought. So, like always, it joined the party and decided to go next time.

Next time, a female technician happened to make a beautiful plate of Aniimo-meal to feed it. “Ugh—saying goodbye now would totally kill the vibe!” So, like always, it finished the pretty meal and decided it would say it next time.

Next time, the time after next... it never seemed like the right moment. Maybe a young operator was crying over a breakup and needed the adorable Morphling to comfort them. Maybe a batch of new hires had just joined Tesella Pod and were building precious friendships with it. Either way, no day felt right—so every day became: “Ugh, next time for sure!”

...

And so, one morning—before the workday even began—the Morphling took off the mask that carried its memories and quietly set it down at Tesella Pod’s front door. With the mask removed, Astra faded from its memory, leaving only a warm, happy blur.

Free at last, the Morphling set out on its journey.

“After the trip is over, I’ll put it back on again!”
